title: One deterministic ARA turn
description: Read the small command-line example as responsibilities, then follow one message through its four capabilities. This is an explanation of the source, not an acceptance proof or a map of deployed ARA Light.

provenance.method: Read-only GitHub source inspection through the connected GitHub tools. Resolved main first, then fetched all cited files at that exact commit. Source-declared behavior and test assertions only.
provenance.limitations: No target code, demo or tests executed. This is not deployed ARA Light or its backend. The test file reimplements a related ara2 graph. Runtime internals, long-lived conversation reuse and production integration are not established by this folder.

nodes.title: Start one example turn
nodes.summary: A command-line entry reads text and calls runAraTurn.
nodes.body: The package's demo script runs src/main.ts. main() reads process.argv[2], or uses “Help me make this practical”, then awaits runAraTurn(text). This is a small command-line example inside vict-02. It is not the deployed ARA Light app or backend.

nodes.title: Configure the runtime
nodes.summary: Register four capabilities and activate one graph.
nodes.body: createAraRuntime creates a VICT runtime, registers the four ARA capabilities, and awaits runtime.activate(araGraph). Failed activation throws with issue messages. runAraTurn calls this setup, then runtime.run({text}), and returns the result plus graph, capability-set and activation versions.

nodes.title: Declare the four-step path
nodes.body: araGraph names the entry user-message, binds four node IDs to their capability IDs, and connects them in a simple chain. It declares topology; implementations live in capabilities.ts. The graph node called assistant is backed by a deterministic function here.

nodes.title: Bind work to contracts
nodes.summary: Each capability states its input, output and effect.
nodes.body: registerAraCapabilities registers user-message, prepare-context, assistant and assistant-response. Three are marked pure. The assistant capability is marked read, but its implementation in this example calls deterministicAssistant; that effect classification does not imply a network model call occurred.

nodes.title: Keep message shapes explicit
nodes.summary: User text → prepared context → assistant message.
nodes.body: contracts.ts opts into the SDK's Zod adapter. The three version-1 contracts declare nonempty input text, text with a string-array context, and a nonempty assistant reply with role 'assistant'. main.ts checks the final output again before printing it.

nodes.title: Generate a deterministic reply
nodes.summary: Same input produces the same local response.
nodes.body: deterministicAssistant trims and normalizes whitespace in the input text, then formats a fixed reply mentioning how many context notes it received. The inspected implementation has no model-provider request. It demonstrates the orchestration shape rather than AI response quality.

nodes.title: Normalize the user text
nodes.summary: The first capability trims the text.
nodes.body: ara.user-message is pure. Its input and output are UserMessageContract; invoke returns {text: input.text.trim()}. araGraph declares it as the entry. This map describes the source-declared path, not a captured execution.

nodes.title: Add two context notes
nodes.summary: Carry text forward with a small context array.
nodes.body: ara.prepare-context is pure. It returns the text and two deterministic notes: a conversation label and the user's goal. There is no repository search, memory service or model context retrieval in this function.

nodes.title: Call the assistant capability
nodes.body: createAssistantCapability declares PreparedContextContract → AssistantMessageContract and effect 'read'. invoke calls the local deterministicAssistant implementation. The source includes no live provider configuration or credentials in this example.

nodes.title: Return the assistant message
nodes.summary: Forward the declared role and text.
nodes.body: ara.assistant-response is pure and has the assistant message contract on both sides. Its invoke returns the incoming role and text, completing the four-node chain.

nodes.title: Validate and print the result
nodes.summary: Print structured text, version identities and ordered events.
nodes.body: After runAraTurn, main requires status completed and a present output. It parses the output using AssistantMessageContract. Failures print an error and exit with code 1. On success it prints the structured response, run ID, topology/capability-set/activation versions and the sequence/type of each event in result.trace.

nodes.title: Read what the tests assert
nodes.summary: Public-surface tests reimplement a related ara2 graph.
nodes.body: public-surface.test.ts builds its own ara2 capabilities and graph against public APIs. It asserts the four-step order, final contract, 13 events and identity fields; it also tests simulation with a registered double. Those are inspected test assertions. I did not execute them or use them as an acceptance verdict for this viewer.

nodes.title: Is setup reused between turns?
nodes.summary: The wrapper constructs a runtime for each runAraTurn call.
nodes.body: Observed call structure: runAraTurn invokes createAraRuntime on each call. The setup comment says compilation is kept out of the conversational hot path, but a long-lived conversation host is not shown in this folder. Whether or how to reuse the activated runtime is a design question for a real application, not something this example establishes.

nodes.title: Keep the example's boundary clear
nodes.summary: A local orchestration example, not ARA Light.
nodes.body: This map explains only examples/ara-proof at the pinned GitHub main commit. It does not establish deployed ARA behavior, live model integration, durable multi-turn chat, or production acceptance. Runtime/compiler internals were not traced exhaustively. No target source was changed and no example command or tests were run.

edges.label: calls
edges.body: main passes one input text to runAraTurn, which configures and runs the example.

edges.label: registers
edges.body: Runtime setup calls registerAraCapabilities before activation.

edges.label: binds
edges.body: Each graph node points to one registered capability ID.

edges.label: declares
edges.body: Capabilities specify these input and output contracts.

edges.label: starts at
edges.body: The entry calls the wrapper; the activated graph declares user-message as its entry. This is the authored behavior path.

edges.label: passes text
edges.body: araGraph routes the user-message output to prepare-context.

edges.label: supplies context
edges.body: The prepared text and two context notes become the assistant capability input.

edges.label: passes reply
edges.body: araGraph routes the assistant message to assistant-response.

edges.label: returns result
edges.body: runtime.run returns to the wrapper and main; main checks and prints the final result.

edges.label: models a variant
edges.body: The public-surface tests declare ara2-proof rather than directly importing araGraph; their assertions are related source evidence, not a runtime observation of this example.

edges.label: questions reuse
edges.body: The wrapper creates its runtime per call; a persistent conversational host is outside this folder.

edges.label: bounds the evidence
edges.body: Reading test source does not establish that those tests passed here.

views.title: What the example contains
views.description: Start at the command line, then distinguish runtime setup, graph, capabilities, contracts and the local reply function.

views.title: Follow one message
views.description: Input → trim → context → deterministic reply → output. Click a connection point to inspect what moves between steps.

views.title: What this leaves open
views.description: Separate source declarations and test assertions from unanswered application questions.
